# C7 — Deployment reliability evidence

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **UNRESOLVED** — An open question, conflict, or missing measurement blocks a stronger statement. |
| Strongest accepted evidence | MODEL ONLY |
| Evidence classes cited | IMPLEMENTATION, TEST PROCEDURE, SIMULATED |
| Gate reached | SOFTWARE REPRODUCTION (next: SYNTHETIC TEST) |
| Last review | CURRENT — snapshot recorded 2026-09-28 by tooling snapshot (no human review) |

**Question.** Does simulated deployment succeed in at least 99.9% of trials under manufacturing tolerances, and is that simulation informative?

**Current statement.** A seeded 10,000-trial deployment simulation records 10,000 successes, and the denominator is now explicit. The model cannot fail its velocity criterion for a locked trial and uses a different fin and speed than C6, so the 100% figure does not discriminate between designs. No physical deployment has been observed.

## Known contradictions

- None on record.

## Open questions

- The success criterion cannot fail for a locked trial, so the result cannot discriminate designs (D-013).

## Discrepancies

- [D-010](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-010) (OPEN) No shared design point across the mass, spring, reliability, and structural models
- [D-013](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-013) (OPEN) The reliability simulation cannot produce the failures it counts
- [D-014](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-014) (RESOLVED) The historical 10,000-trial summary could not be reconstructed from its CSV

## Assumptions

- A reliability statement needs a trial count, seed, model revision, and outcome definition.

## Limitations

- Simulation outcomes do not measure physical reliability.
- No empirical confidence bound is asserted.
- The simulated fin, speed, and spring treatment differ from C6 (D-010, D-013).

## Measurement needed to close the next gate

- A reviewed model whose failure modes can occur, run at the shared design point.
- Repeated inert deployment trials of a physical mechanism once C1 is resolved.

## Pre-registered experiments

- None.

## What this claim does not establish

- Any inert physical measurement: none has been accepted for this claim.
- Physical performance of any hardware.
- Flight readiness or safety for live propulsion.
